html:
Naadam is Mongolia's great summer festival of the "three games of men": wrestling, horse racing and archery. In 1912, soon after Mongolia declared independence from the Qing under the Bogd Khan, it became a yearly festival of the new state.

The games are much older. Steppe peoples held such contests at gatherings and religious feasts, and wrestling, riding and shooting were the skills of every warrior of the Mongol Empire.

After the revolution of 1921, the national Naadam was moved to 11 July, the anniversary of the revolution, and it is still held then in Ulaanbaatar. Wrestlers in short jackets and pointed boots compete for titles such as "lion" and "titan". In the horse races, child jockeys ride across tens of kilometres of open steppe. Women now compete in archery and horse racing. UNESCO listed Naadam as world heritage in 2010.
